newsitem.title: LEBANON: Amnesty wants Israeli ally to free student.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty wants Israeli ally to free student.

text.p: Amnesty International called on Thursday for the immediate release of a Lebanese man it said was held by a pro-Israeli militia in south Lebanon if he was not charged with criminal offences.

The international human rights organisation said Ahmad Kamil Sa'id, a secondary school student held on June 2 in Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, should be granted access to his lawyer, family, doctor and the International Committee of the Red Cross.

In a statement faxed to an international news agency in Beirut, Amnesty urged people to write to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and General Antoine Lahd, commander of the pro-Israeli militia in south Lebanon, to seek assurances that Sa'id "is not being tortured or ill-treated".
Sa'id should be immediately released "if he is not promptly charged with a recognizable criminal offence and tried before a court which meets international standards for fair trials," Amnesty said.

About 130 Lebanese and other Arabs are held by Lahd's South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia at a hilltop jail at Khiam in the border strip occupied by Israel since 1978. None of the prisoners has been charged with any offence or tried.
